name: Booking
description: Generic appointment and resource scheduling: services, providers/staff or resources, availability rules and exceptions, time-slot booking with buffers and capacity, recurrence, reminders, cancellation policy, and calendar sync. Other domains (restaurant, hospitality) may depend on this instead of duplicating slot/availability logic.

sources.title: Cal.diy (Cal.com's open-source community edition)
sources.notes: Not cloned (monorepo, 1.1GB, exceeds practical clone cost for this pass; inspected via raw.githubusercontent.com Prisma schema). Root LICENSE file verified as MIT, 2026-09-26 — the repository's own README states it is 'Cal.diy', a fork of Cal.com with all enterprise/commercial code removed and '100% MIT-licensed, no Open Core split'. This CORRECTS an initial assumption (carried in the task brief) that calcom/cal.com is AGPL: that historically described Cal.com's paid/Enterprise-Edition core, which is not what this repository now contains. Permissive license means it is not marked reference-only for licensing reasons, though nothing was copied — only entity/field names were read from packages/prisma/schema.prisma (EventType, Booking, Attendee, Host, Schedule, Availability, OutOfOfficeEntry, BookingSeat, BookingReference, Payment, Webhook).

sources.title: Easy!Appointments
sources.notes: Not cloned (inspected via raw.githubusercontent.com README + openapi.yml). GPL-3.0 verified from actual LICENSE file. Reference-only, no code copied. Its own OpenAPI contract (openapi.yml) confirms: appointments, availabilities, unavailabilities, customers, services, service_categories, providers, secretaries (a scheduling-on-behalf-of role), working_plan_exceptions, blocked_periods, webhooks. README notes some capabilities (e.g. SMS reminders, deposits) may be gated behind a paid 'premium' tier, not confirmed present in the open-source core — flagged per-feature below.

sources.title: RFC 5545 — Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar)
sources.license: IETF Trust — freely usable/implementable per BCP 78/79
sources.notes: Authoritative standard for calendar events, recurrence rules (RRULE), and time-zone handling; the canonical reference for recurring bookings and calendar sync/export.

sources.title: Wikipedia: No-show (booking)
sources.notes: General background for no-show policy; used only where not directly evidenced in the two inspected implementations.

sources.title: PCI Data Security Standard v4.0.1
sources.license: PCI SSC copyright; free to read/download with registration
sources.notes: Same standard already verified for domains/restaurant and domains/hospitality; applies identically to any booking product collecting card deposits/payments.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Resource allocation
sources.notes: General background for non-human bookable resources (rooms, equipment); neither Cal.diy nor Easy!Appointments models a generic resource entity.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Waiting list
sources.notes: General background for booking waitlists; not present in either inspected implementation.

features.name: Services
features.description: A bookable offering with a name, duration, and price (e.g. '30-minute consultation').

provenance.notes: Downgraded high→medium on 2026-09-27: fewer than 3 implementations and no authoritative source.

features.name: Providers / staff
features.description: The person (or team member) who performs a service and owns a schedule.

provenance.notes: Downgraded high→medium on 2026-09-27: fewer than 3 implementations and no authoritative source.

features.name: Bookable resources
features.description: A non-human bookable unit (room, equipment, vehicle) with its own availability, alongside or instead of a provider.

provenance.notes: Neither Cal.diy nor Easy!Appointments models a generic non-human bookable resource — both are provider/host-centric. Included as a common pattern in resource-scheduling products generally (e.g. room/equipment booking), not corroborated by an inspected implementation.

features.name: Availability rules / working hours
features.description: A provider's (or resource's) recurring weekly working hours, from which bookable time slots are derived.

provenance.notes: Downgraded high→medium on 2026-09-27: fewer than 3 implementations and no authoritative source.

features.name: Availability exceptions
features.description: One-off overrides to the normal schedule for a specific date: holidays, custom hours, or extra availability.

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's Availability.date field and OutOfOfficeEntry; Easy!Appointments' working_plan_exceptions endpoint. Downgraded high→medium on 2026-09-27: fewer than 3 implementations and no authoritative source.

features.name: Time slot computation
features.description: Derive bookable start times from availability rules, existing bookings, buffers, and slot interval.

provenance.notes: Downgraded high→medium on 2026-09-27: fewer than 3 implementations and no authoritative source.

features.name: Buffers
features.description: Padding time before and/or after a booking during which the provider/resource is not bookable.

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's EventType.beforeEventBuffer/afterEventBuffer are explicit; Easy!Appointments' openapi.yml has no equivalent field in the inspected schema, though its README mentions 'breaks' at the provider working-plan level, which is a related but distinct concept.

features.name: Bookings / appointments
features.description: A confirmed reservation of a service with a provider (and/or resource) for a specific time slot.

provenance.notes: Downgraded high→medium on 2026-09-27: fewer than 3 implementations and no authoritative source.

features.name: Recurring bookings
features.description: Book the same service/slot on a repeating schedule (weekly, monthly) as a linked series.

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's EventType.recurringEvent and Booking.recurringEventId confirm the implementation; RFC 5545 RRULE is the authoritative recurrence-rule model most such implementations converge on (not verified that Cal.diy's JSON format follows RRULE literally). Not found in Easy!Appointments' inspected API surface.

features.name: Group bookings / shared capacity
features.description: Allow multiple attendees to book the same time slot up to a capacity limit (e.g. a class or webinar).

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's EventType.seatsPerTimeSlot + BookingSeat are explicit; Easy!Appointments' ServiceRecord.attendantsNumber is the equivalent field. Corroborated by both.

features.name: Reminders
features.description: Automated email/SMS reminders sent ahead of a booking.

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's Booking.smsReminderNumber field and ReminderMail model confirm this. Easy!Appointments' README lists an 'email notification system' for confirmations but its README flags reminders/SMS as potentially premium-tier; not confirmed present in the open-source core.

features.name: Cancellation and no-show policies
features.description: Rules for how and when a booking can be cancelled or rescheduled, and how a no-show is recorded.

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's Booking.cancellationReason/rejectionReason and BookingStatus enum (cancelled/rejected/accepted/pending) confirm cancellation and rejection tracking; no explicit no-show status was found in either implementation's inspected schema (Easy!Appointments' AppointmentRecord.status was not enumerated in this pass).

features.name: Minimum booking notice
features.description: A minimum lead time required between booking and the appointment start (blocks last-minute bookings).

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's EventType.minimumBookingNotice is explicit; no equivalent field found in Easy!Appointments' inspected API surface.

features.name: Deposits and paid bookings
features.description: Collect a payment or deposit at the time of booking.

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's Booking.paid flag and Payment model confirm this. Easy!Appointments' README flags deposits/payments as likely premium-tier; not confirmed present in its open-source core.

features.name: Calendar sync
features.description: Two-way sync of bookings with an external calendar (Google Calendar, Outlook, CalDAV).

features.name: Out-of-office / blocked time
features.description: Mark a provider unavailable for a date range (vacation, sick leave), blocking new bookings.

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's OutOfOfficeEntry (with optional reassignment to another user) and Easy!Appointments' Unavailability/blocked_periods endpoints both confirm this. Downgraded high→medium on 2026-09-27: fewer than 3 implementations and no authoritative source.

features.name: Embeddable booking widget / public link
features.description: A public, shareable booking page or embeddable widget for a service or provider.

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's HashedLink model (private booking links) and its core public-booking-page product concept confirm this; not found in Easy!Appointments' inspected API surface, though it is a self-hosted booking form by design.

features.name: Booking webhooks
features.description: Fire outbound events (booking created/cancelled/rescheduled) to external systems.

provenance.notes: Both Cal.diy (Webhook model, WebhookScheduledTriggers) and Easy!Appointments (webhooks endpoint with actions + secretToken) confirm this. Downgraded high→medium on 2026-09-27: fewer than 3 implementations and no authoritative source.

features.name: Teams and round-robin assignment
features.description: Assign a booking to one of several providers on a team, by availability, priority, or round robin.

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's Host model (isFixed, priority, weight per event type) and Easy!Appointments' Secretary-manages-Providers model both show provider-team assignment concepts, though the specific mechanisms differ (round-robin/weighted vs. delegated scheduling).

features.name: Manual booking approval
features.description: Require a provider or manager to approve a requested booking before it is confirmed.

provenance.notes: Cal.diy's BookingStatus includes PENDING and AWAITING_HOST alongside ACCEPTED/REJECTED, confirming an approval step exists; not found in Easy!Appointments' inspected schema.

features.name: Booking waitlist
features.description: Let a customer join a waitlist for a fully booked slot and be notified if it opens up.

provenance.notes: Not found in either inspected implementation; reasoned from common scheduling-product practice.

features.name: Timezone-aware scheduling
features.description: Display and book slots correctly across the customer's and provider's timezones.
